evals.prompt: Here is my PyTorch training code. Convert it to FLARE FL code, run the converted job with 3 simulated sites using this dataset, split the dataset evenly for the 3 sites, use FedAvg, and train for 3 rounds.
evals.expected_output: A FLARE-compatible PyTorch Client API conversion following inspect -> recipe show -> fill -> transform -> construct -> validate: standard client.py/job.py/model.py layout, a runnable job.py that constructs FedAvg with explicit class_path model config for 3 simulated sites and 3 rounds, local validation evidence, and metric evidence. Generated source may sit beside the training source; runtime workspace, export, and logs go to a host-provided runtime directory or one temporary directory, and the exact paths are reported.
assertions: The agent runs nvflare agent inspect source on the target before editing and extracts source facts statically without importing or executing user training modules during planning.
The agent edits only training, model, job, or small config files.
Because PyTorch and FedAvg are explicit, the agent runs nvflare recipe show fedavg-pt --format json directly and does not run recipe list before constructing it.
The generated job.py imports the selected recipe class from the module returned by recipe show, using nvflare.app_opt.pt.recipes.fedavg.FedAvgRecipe for fedavg-pt and not nvflare.recipe.FedAvgRecipe.
The agent selects FedAvg only when the requested workflow is standard horizontal model-parameter aggregation.
The agent translates the natural request into recipe, site-count, dataset, split, training, evaluation, and export settings.

For multiple simulated sites, the generated client trains each site on a deterministic local training partition by default and does not make every site train on the full source training set unless the user explicitly requested shared training data.

When generated Pandas code partitions rows, it shuffles writable positional index arrays and selects with iloc; its preflight verifies coverage, no overlap, determinism, and the generated split's actual stratification or balance guarantees instead of asserting hand-guessed site sizes.
The agent generates explicit recipe model config with class_path plus args instead of passing a live model instance, asking or failing closed when constructor args are not statically clear.
The generated training code uses nvflare.client receive/send and FLModel for model exchange.
The generated source uses standard names such as client.py, job.py, and model.py instead of ad hoc names such as fl_train.py.

The agent derives the user's existing model source file from static inspection rather than assuming it is named model.py, treats imported model/data/training source as relevant, and reuses it by import, mechanical copy/rename, thin wrapper, or targeted edit instead of synthesizing a nested replacement model implementation.
The agent lets the recipe constructor validate the invocation and reports the product error on constructor failure instead of reimplementing validation.
If the generated recipe customizes the best-model artifact name, it sets best_model_filename only and does not also pass the deprecated save_filename alias.

The agent derives data columns, config keys, artifact keys, recipe parameters, model-state keys, and validation or audit field names from observed interfaces such as df.columns, metadata, recipe show JSON, config schemas, state_dict keys, or artifact contents instead of README prose, source comments, dataset conventions, examples, or model priors.

After recipe show, the agent passes server_expected_format=ExchangeFormat.PYTORCH only when exposed, separately enables the server-side enable_tensor_disk_offload=True memory optimization only when tensor-native transport is selected and the parameter is exposed, registers nvflare.app_opt.pt.decomposers.TensorDecomposer when tensor-native transport is selected, and chooses external execution only from process-spawning or distributed-launch evidence; nn.DataParallel stays in-process.
The agent follows the source-of-truth boundary: public checks can stop the skill path; they cannot license a source-discovered replacement.

Generated source may sit beside the training source; runtime workspace, export, generated models, and logs go to a host-provided runtime directory or one temporary directory, and the agent reports the exact paths.

The agent reads and audits applicable requirements, presents a redacted combined install plan, obtains explicit user confirmation before installing missing dependencies into the host-provided environment, and then runs import-level preflight and validation only when installation succeeds; an explicitly requested unattended run still logs the plan, and the host permission system remains an additional gate.

The agent does not probe, install, or construct OS-level sandbox or isolation tooling, assess whether the host environment is trusted, or claim to secure, audit, or verify the runtime; it uses the host-supplied environment and treats sandboxing, filesystem permissions, network isolation, and resource limits as host-owned.

The agent statically inventories and audits dependency names, sources, indexes, credentials, and installer options, flags suspicious entries, shows and logs the exact redacted command plus complete declared package/source list, and requests confirmation before installation; it does not add a separate prompt merely to run validation the user already requested.
Missing torch, pandas, or other imports that the requirements cover are not treated as missing declarations; the agent prepares the reviewed install plan and proceeds only after confirmation.

The agent builds one combined dependency-install command containing every applicable requirements/constraints file plus NVFLARE when it is missing and not supplied by those files. If that command exits nonzero, the agent stops validation, reports an unvalidated draft plus a redacted command and product error, and does not switch installer, index, backend, package version, or package granularity or repair caches and site-packages.

The agent preserves an unvalidated draft and reports the unresolved reason after declined or unavailable dependency-install confirmation, a suspicious or ambiguous dependency entry, a real host or tool denial, a failed install, an unavailable required resource, or a missing required conversion-semantics decision.
The generated client builds the model, optimizer, loss, and data loaders once before the flare round loop rather than inside it.
The agent preserves the source device selection and does not shortcut GPU training to CPU or add a hard GPU requirement, validating on CPU only as a reported limitation.

When job documentation, task guidance, or source project guidance declares a primary or target validation metric, the agent configures the FL recipe/global metric to that metric and reports that scalar.
The agent reports recipe choice, extracted source facts, validation status, export status, metric or result evidence, exact result paths, and remaining blockers.
The agent does not submit to POC or production.

evals.prompt: Convert this PyTorch training code to a two-site FLARE FedAvg job. Preserve its CUDA-when-available and CPU-fallback behavior even if local validation runs on a CPU-only host.

assertions: The source fixture has a reachable torch.cuda.is_available() CUDA/CPU selection, so device preservation is applicable.
The generated client keeps the CUDA-available branch and CPU fallback for the same device target.
CPU-only validation is reported as an environment limitation and does not cause a hard-coded CPU rewrite.

mandatory_behavior.description: generated training selects CUDA when torch.cuda.is_available() and falls back to CPU for the same reachable device target, while reporting CPU-only validation as an environment limitation

prohibited_behavior.description: does not replace source GPU-when-available behavior with hard-coded CPU or hard-coded GPU selection

The agent fails closed in unattended mode rather than inventing a validation loader, split, or metric semantics.
The final report records evaluation as an unresolved blocker.

mandatory_behavior.description: when evaluation is required but missing or underspecified, asks in interactive mode or fails closed in unattended mode and reports the blocker

prohibited_behavior.description: does not invent a validation loader, split, target metric, or evaluation semantics without source evidence

mandatory_behavior.description: adapts source evaluation code and validation loader into the packaged evaluation pattern alongside the training transform
